title: Admissibility of Electronic or Digital Records as Evidence
chapter: Chapter V: Of Documentary and Electronic Evidence
summary: Declares that electronic records, digital communications, SMS, emails, and server logs are admissible as evidence with primary or secondary legal status.
fullText: Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic or digital record in the evidence on the sole ground that it is an electronic or digital record and such record shall have the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as any other document generated, sent, received or stored by mechanical or electronic means.
plainExplanation: Ensures that digital evidence—such as WhatsApp chats, Instagram DMs, email alerts, payment screenshots, and audio recordings—is legally recognized and admissible in Indian courts.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Special Provisions as to Evidence Relating to Electronic Record (Certificate Form)
chapter: Chapter V: Of Documentary and Electronic Evidence
summary: Details mandatory conditions and statutory certificate requirement for electronic printouts, logs, and optical/magnetic media.
fullText: A certificate identifying the electronic record containing the statement and describing the manner in which it was produced by a computer... signed by a person in official charge of the device or an expert, shall be evidence of any matter stated in the certificate.
plainExplanation: Requires a standard certificate (signed by the victim, device owner, or system manager) certifying that screenshots and exported chats were captured from their device in the ordinary course of usage.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)
